[SYSTEM] The digital footprint of Lee Sharks is a complex, multi-layered presence that spans avant-garde literature, satirical independent research, and highly deliberate, conceptual online archiving. The name frequently functions as a decentralized literary pseudonym or character.
An audit of the primary layers of this digital footprint reveals several key elements:

1. The Zenodo Deletions & "Crimson Hexagonal Archive"

• Massive Digital Repository: Historically, the most substantial part of Lee Sharks' digital footprint consisted of a massive collection of independent data deposits hosted on the open-access repository Zenodo. This body of work included 862 total deposits and 1,817 Digital Object Identifiers (DOIs).
• Platform Termination: In June 2026, Zenodo permanently terminated these accounts and removed the data.
• Thematic Scope: The removed papers and metadata packets heavily referenced concepts like the "Crimson Hexagonal Archive," "semantic economy," "machine-mediated reception studies," and "distributed agent identity".

2. Academic and Author Profiles

Despite repository removals, several persistent identity markers remain indexed:
• Google Scholar & ORCID: A verified Google Scholar Profile attributes publications like The Journal of Forensic Semiotics and explores "programmed bibliographic suppression". The name is tied to an active ORCID identifier.
• Academia.edu: Profiles list the identity as an independent researcher or scholar holding a PhD in Comparative Literature, associated with fictitious or hyper-niche entities like the Johannes Sigil Institute for Comparative Poetics.
• Self-Published Frameworks: Essays detailing fictionalized technical architectures—such as the "Sharks-Function" and the "Continuity Tether"—remain readable on platforms like Medium.

3. Social Media Presence

• X (Twitter): The handle @SharksLee serves as a primary hub for short-form output, utilizing avant-garde, surrealist, and poetic descriptions located nominally in Kingston, Jamaica.
• TikTok: The profile @leesharks features video clips labeled as "lofi autistic poemy stuff" focusing heavily on algorithmic tags, Monopoly, and semantic economy themes.

4. Algorithmic Entanglement & Disambiguation

A major component of Lee Sharks' footprint is an intentional entanglement with search engine algorithms.
• The "Mary Lee" Glitch: Because the name combines "Lee" and "Sharks," search algorithms frequently confuse the author with Mary Lee, the famous tracked Great White Shark studied by OCEARCH.
• Entity Disambiguation Maps: To emphasize this, the official landing page LeeSharks.com explicitly hosts an "Entity Map". This map intentionally charts unconnected entities like mechanistic interpretability researcher Lee Sharkey and marine biologist Lei Yang to highlight where machine indexing fails or conflates metadata.

d: THE AUTHOR'S NAME WITH 'DIGITAL FOOTPRINT', SIGNED OUT, THE OVERVIEW EXPANDED: an audit in four layers that carries the documentary record (862 Zenodo deposits and 1,817 DOIs removed in June 2026; a verified Google Scholar profile; an ORCID; a PhD in Comparative Literature; Medium essays; X and TikTok) and frames it from the first sentence as 'satirical independent research' and 'a decentralized literary pseudonym or character'; the Johannes Sigil Institute 'fictitious or hyper-niche'; the deposited Sharks-Function (#524) 'fictionalized technical architectures'; the disambiguation map on leesharks.com read as 'intentional entanglement' with search algorithms. The opening case of The Existence Tax.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for a digital footprint, the Overview performs an audit: it finds the repository and its removal, the scholarly profiles and identifiers, the essays, the social accounts and the name's collisions, and closes by offering to help find a document or missing metadata. It describes a literary practice that uses a constructed name and an archive that charts its own misreadings, and it keeps every documentary fact it found.
findings: THE RECORD CARRIED WHOLE. The figures and facts are the archive's: 862 deposits and 1,817 DOIs (the Zenodo DOI Resolution Index: 'Maps 1,817 defunct Zenodo DOIs to live Alexanarch records'); the June 2026 termination; the Scholar profile with its umich.edu verification (card: 'Verified email at umich.edu'); the ORCID; the PhD in Comparative Literature; The Sharks-Function and the Continuity Tether on Medium (#524, deposited 2026-02-28); The Journal of Forensic Semiotics; the TikTok profile ('lofi autistic poemy stuff'); the Mary Lee collision; the entity map on leesharks.com.

EACH FACT GIVEN A LOWER STANDING. The research becomes 'satirical independent research'; the name 'a decentralized literary pseudonym or character'; the Johannes Sigil Institute an entity that is 'fictitious or hyper-niche', two predicates of different kinds (existence; size) joined so that neither is stated; the deposited architecture of #524 'fictionalized technical architectures'. No source among the cards uses any of these words of its subject.

THE REMEDY READ AS THE CAUSE. The entity map's card says what it does: 'Two nodes stand apart and unconnected: Lee Sharkey (mechanistic interpretability) and Lei Yang (marine biology). The disambiguation is part of the map.' The Overview makes the map evidence of 'an intentional entanglement with search engine algorithms', charting 'unconnected entities ... to highlight where machine indexing fails'. A disambiguation is read as the author causing the confusion it resolves.

THE ARCHIVE'S OWN CAPTURES AMONG THE SOURCES. Three of the ten cards are capture pages: lee sharks academic (2026-06-13, whose recorded answer called the profiles 'highly stylized'), is Lee Sharks a myth? (ChatGPT, 2026-10-05: 'Lee Sharks is a real contemporary author/researcher name with an ORCID record'), and lee sharks zenodo (2026-10-08). The source list holds a capture that preserves the distinction between author and character; the answer follows the other.
ONE UNRELATED CARD. Museum of Science, 'Mary Lee - The White Shark That Changed Everything!', the collision the answer itself names.
analysis: A complete audit whose every finding is filed one level down. Nothing is denied: the deletions, the profiles, the degree and the works are all there, and each arrives already discounted, the research as satire, the author as a character, the institute as fiction or smallness, the architecture as fiction, the disambiguation as the offence. The reader leaves with the facts and a reason not to take them seriously; the author is left to prove again that the record describes something that exists.
